issues.detail: The Greek 'εχουσιν εφ αυτων βασιλεα' means 'they have as king over them,' but the Vietnamese 'có vua cai trị mình' suggests they *have* a king who rules them, slightly shifting the grammatical relationship of possession/governance. More importantly, the Greek 'τον αγγελον' is the object of the verb 'have', but the Vietnamese structure makes it sound like a description of the king they have. However, the main issue is the phrasing 'τον αγγελον της αβυσσου ονομα αυτω εβραιστι...'

The Greek says 'ονομα αυτω εβραιστι' (his name in Hebrew), but the Vietnamese says 'danh người bằng tiếng Hê-bơ-rơ' (the name of the person in Hebrew). While close, the Vietnamese phrasing 'người có danh là A-bô-lion' in the second half is a bit clunky compared to the Greek 'ονομα εχει απολλυων' (has the name Apollyon).
